newsitem.title: THAILAND: Chavalit key Thai player in or out of uniform.
newsitem.headline: Chavalit key Thai player in or out of uniform.

text.p: General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, named Thailand's 22nd prime minister on Monday, has been an orchestrator of Thai politics for decades both in and out of uniform with an eye on the nation's top job for many years.

A former army chief and defence minister in outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa's coalition government, Chavalit now heads the New Aspiration Party (NAP) which he founded in 1990 after retiring from the military.
The NAP won a slim two-seat victory in a November 17 general election and has formed a six-party coalition government.

Chavalit's party was a partner in the past two governments, and he served as deputy prime minister in both. He was Defence Minister in Banharn's cabinet and Interior Minister in the previous adminstration of Democrat premier Chuan Leekpai.
Since being named Defence Minister after the July, 1995, general election, the quietly ambitious Chavalit, 64, was often touted as a candidate for prime minister.

He used the defence portfolio to strengthen his own power base, by dabbling in military reshuffles to place loyal officers in key positions and supporting big-budget military procurement to satisfy the armed forces.

In the last election campaign, Chavalit wooed many strong politicians from other parties to defect to his NAP. Some opposition parties accused the cash-rich NAP of enticing them with money, but Chavalit denied the charge.
Chavalit, who had made no secret of his ambition to become prime minister, has said he was a behind-the-scenes power broker for too long and wanted a chance to lead the country.
"I have given chances (to be prime minister) to somebody else for the last 35 years already. This country needs repair, it needs leadership," he told Reuters in a recent interview.

Chavalit claimed he was behind former prime minister General Prem Tinsulananda's ascendency to the premiership in 1980. He also said he was instrumental in enabling ex-diplomat General Chatichai Choonhavan to become prime minister in 1988.

Born in Bangkok's neighbouring Nonthaburi province in 1932, Chavalit began his career as a professional soldier on entering Chulachomklao Royal Military Academy in 1953. He also received staff training in Thailand and the United States.
Chavalit built his reputation on a successful "hearts and minds" campaign which brought Thai communist insurgents of the 1970s and early 1980s out of the jungle.
In the 1960s, he was operations and training officer for Thai troops fighting with the U.S.-backed forces in South Vietnam.

As a powerful army chief and supreme commander of the armed forces in 1986, General Chavalit wielded political power traditionally held by the military while at the same time stressing a vision of a democratic country in which soldiers would no longer hold sway over civilian rule.
He concentrated on unifying the army and stopping officer cliques from meddling in politics. The armed forces retained an important say but it spoke with a single voice -- Chavalit's.
He has also attacked corruption among politicians and businessmen as a fatal flaw in Thai society.
He has written heavily about the need for a country that has seen 17 military coups or attempted coups to complete a democratic revolution.
